2. **`countable_set_measure_support`**

3. **`GrpCat_Uncountable`**

**Mathematical statement:**  
The set of all nonempty subsets of the collection of all groups is not a measurable set when the power set is equipped with the product sigma-algebra (generated by the “belongs to” projections for every group). More generally, for any uncountable set, the subset of its power set consisting of the nonempty subsets is never in the product sigma-algebra.

Imagine you have a way of “measuring” a subset of groups by checking membership for each group individually, as in a product space of coin flips. The question “is the subset nonempty?” would require you to know whether there exists at least one group in it. However, any measurable event in the product sigma-algebra can only depend on countably many coordinates (groups). Since there are uncountably many groups, there is always a group you didn’t examine, so you can never be certain whether the subset is empty or not—you cannot make that decision with only countable information. Hence the collection of nonempty subsets is not measurable.
